```{r rolling-salience-band-gaps}
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "100%"

# --- Five-term rolling salience-band gaps ------------------------------------

rolling_years <- seq.int(analysis_start_term, analysis_end_term)

rolling_lookback <- rolling_window_terms - 1L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimum sample size for displayed rolling estimates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

min_cases_for_plot <- 5L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mutually exclusive salience bands
#
# CSI < 2 is the common low-salience reference group.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

salience_band_levels <- c("CSI < 2", "CSI 2-4", "CSI 5-6", "CSI >= 7")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rolling appointing-party alignment by salience band
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rolling_Phi_Bands <- purrr::map_dfr(
  rolling_years, function(t) {
    
    window_start <- max(analysis_start_term, t - rolling_lookback)
    
    x <- SCOTUS_Contested %>%
      dplyr::filter(term >= window_start, term <= t) %>% dplyr::mutate(
        
        Salience_Band = dplyr::case_when(
            csi < 2                    ~ "CSI < 2",
            csi >= 2 & csi < 5         ~ "CSI 2-4",
            csi >= 5 & csi < 7         ~ "CSI 5-6",
            csi >= 7                   ~ "CSI >= 7",
            TRUE                       ~ NA_character_))
    
    band_summary <- x %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(Salience_Band)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Salience_Band) %>% dplyr::summarise(
        
        N_Cases = dplyr::n(),
        
        Mean_Phi = safe_mean(phi_abs),
        
        Mean_Phi_Normalized = safe_mean(phi_normalized),
        
        Strict_Split_Rate = safe_rate(strict_party_split),
        
        .groups = "drop")
    
    tibble::tibble(Salience_Band = salience_band_levels) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(band_summary, by = "Salience_Band") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        
        N_Cases = tidyr::replace_na(N_Cases, 0L),
        
        Year = t,
        
        Window_Start = window_start,
        
        Window_End = t,
        
        N_Terms = t - window_start + 1L)
  })

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convert band estimates to wide form
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rolling_Phi_BandGaps <- Rolling_Phi_Bands %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Band_ID = dplyr::case_when(
        Salience_Band == "CSI < 2"  ~ "lt2",
        Salience_Band == "CSI 2-4"  ~ "b24",
        Salience_Band == "CSI 5-6"  ~ "b56",
        Salience_Band == "CSI >= 7" ~ "ge7",
        TRUE                        ~ NA_character_)) %>% dplyr::select(
    Year, Window_Start, Window_End, N_Terms, Band_ID, N_Cases, Mean_Phi,
    Mean_Phi_Normalized, Strict_Split_Rate) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Band_ID, values_from = c(
      N_Cases, Mean_Phi, Mean_Phi_Normalized, Strict_Split_Rate))

Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  # CSI 2-4 relative to CSI < 2
  Rolling_Phi_BandGaps %>% dplyr::transmute(
      
      Year, Window_Start, Window_End, N_Terms,
      
      Series = "CSI 2-4",
      
      N_Cases_Reference = N_Cases_lt2,
      
      N_Cases_Comparison = N_Cases_b24,
      
      Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases_lt2 >= min_cases_for_plot &
        N_Cases_b24 >= min_cases_for_plot,
      
      Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_b24 - Mean_Phi_lt2,
      
      Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_b24 -
        Mean_Phi_Normalized_lt2,
      
      Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_b24 - Strict_Split_Rate_lt2),
  
  # CSI 5-6 relative to CSI < 2
  Rolling_Phi_BandGaps %>% dplyr::transmute(
      
      Year, Window_Start, Window_End, N_Terms,
      
      Series = "CSI 5-6",
      
      N_Cases_Reference = N_Cases_lt2,
      
      N_Cases_Comparison = N_Cases_b56,
      
      Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases_lt2 >= min_cases_for_plot &
        N_Cases_b56 >= min_cases_for_plot,
      
      Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_b56 - Mean_Phi_lt2,
      
      Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_b56 -
        Mean_Phi_Normalized_lt2,
      
      Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_b56 - Strict_Split_Rate_lt2),
  
  Rolling_Phi_BandGaps %>% dplyr::transmute(
      
      Year, Window_Start, Window_End, N_Terms,
      
      Series = "CSI >= 7",
      
      N_Cases_Reference = N_Cases_lt2,
      
      N_Cases_Comparison = N_Cases_ge7,
      
      Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases_lt2 >= min_cases_for_plot &
        N_Cases_ge7 >= min_cases_for_plot,
      
      Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_ge7 - Mean_Phi_lt2,
      
      Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_ge7 -
        Mean_Phi_Normalized_lt2,
      
      Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_ge7 - Strict_Split_Rate_lt2)
) %>% tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Phi_Gap, Phi_Normalized_Gap), names_to = "Gap_Measure",
    values_to = "Gap_Value") %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Gap_Measure = dplyr::recode(
        Gap_Measure, Phi_Gap = "Mean absolute phi gap", Phi_Normalized_Gap =
          "Mean margin-normalized phi gap"),
    
    Gap_Measure = factor(
        Gap_Measure, levels = c(
          "Mean absolute phi gap", "Mean margin-normalized phi gap")),
    
    Gap_Value_Plot = dplyr::if_else(
        Eligible_For_Plot & !is.na(Gap_Value), Gap_Value, NA_real_))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Series ordering
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

band_gap_series_levels <- c("CSI 2-4", "CSI 5-6", "CSI >= 7")

Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long <- Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Series = factor(Series, levels = band_gap_series_levels)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Gap_Measure, Series) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Year, .by_group = TRUE) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Gap_Available = !is.na(Gap_Value_Plot),
    
    Plot_Run = cumsum(
        Gap_Available != dplyr::lag(
            Gap_Available, default = dplyr::first(Gap_Available)))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Salience-band colors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

band_gap_colors <- c(
  "CSI 2-4"  = "#B8C95A", "CSI 5-6"  = "#E9962F", "CSI >= 7" = "#9E0142")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared salience-gap scales and theme
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

phi_band_gap_scales <- list(
  
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Gap_Measure, ncol = 1),
  
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = band_gap_colors, breaks = band_gap_series_levels, labels =
      band_gap_series_levels, name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
  
  ggplot2::guides(
    color = ggplot2::guide_legend(
        nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE, override.aes =
          list(linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 1))),
  
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(analysis_start_term, analysis_end_term),
    breaks = seq(1960, 2020, by = 10),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0))),
  
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(-0.3, -0.15, 0, 0.15, 0.3),
    expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))),
  
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.3, 0.3)),
  
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Salience gaps in appointing-party alignment", x = "Year", y =
      "Difference from CSI < 2 in phi coefficient"),
  
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(),
  
  ggplot2::theme(
    
    legend.position = "bottom",
    
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines"),
    
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    axis.title.x =
      ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 10)),
    
    axis.title.y =
      ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 10)),
    
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Salience-band gap figure without Natural Court shading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_phi_band_gap <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.30) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Gap_Value_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE)), color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.05, alpha = 0.90, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Gap_Value_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE), color = Series),
    linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 0.97, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  phi_band_gap_scales

print(p_phi_band_gap)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "02_phi_rolling_salience_band_gap.emf"),
  plot = p_phi_band_gap, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height = 6.8,
  units = "in")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. Salience-band gap figure with Natural Court composition shading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_phi_band_gap_shaded <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  
  ggplot2::geom_rect(
    data = NaturalCourt_Shading, ggplot2::aes(
      xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
      fill = Shade_Colour, alpha = Shade_Intensity), inherit.aes = FALSE
) +
  
  ggplot2::scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
  
  ggplot2::scale_alpha_identity(guide = "none") +
  
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.30) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Gap_Value_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE)), color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.05, alpha = 0.90, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Phi_BandGaps_Long, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Gap_Value_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE), color = Series),
    linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 0.97, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  phi_band_gap_scales

print(p_phi_band_gap_shaded)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    fig_dir, "02_phi_rolling_salience_band_gap_shaded.emf"), plot =
    p_phi_band_gap_shaded, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height = 6.8,
  units = "in")
```

## Pre-/Post-2010 Descriptive Comparison

### Purpose

The following code presents the descriptive comparison of appointing-party alignment before and after OT2010 in publication-ready form.

The first table reports the underlying alignment levels for high- and lower-salience contested cases at each CSI cutoff. Raw absolute phi and margin-normalized phi are presented side by side, together with the number of cases and the strict appointing-party split rate.

The second table reports the high-minus-low salience gap. To keep the table narrow and readable, the three outcome measures are placed in a long format, with pre-2010, post-2010, and change columns rather than a very wide set of machine-style variable names.

### Created objects

- **PrePost_Phi_Table** — reader-facing table of high- and lower-salience alignment levels before and after 2010.

- **PrePost_Gaps_Table** — reader-facing table of pre-2010, post-2010, and change-in-gap estimates for raw phi, normalized phi, and strict appointing-party splits.

```{r pre-post-2010-comparison}

# --- Pre-/post-2010 descriptive comparison ----------------------------------

PrePost_Phi <- purrr::map_dfr(
  csi_cutoffs, function(k) {
    
    SCOTUS_Contested %>% dplyr::mutate(
        
        Era = dplyr::if_else(term <= 2009, "Pre2010", "Post2010"),
        
        Salience_Group = dplyr::if_else(csi >= k, "High", "Low")) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Era, Salience_Group) %>% dplyr::summarise(
        
        N_Cases = dplyr::n(),
        
        Mean_Phi = safe_mean(phi_abs),
        
        Mean_Phi_Normalized = safe_mean(phi_normalized),
        
        Strict_Split_Rate = safe_rate(strict_party_split),
        
        .groups = "drop") %>% dplyr::mutate(CSI_Cutoff = k)
  })

PrePost_Gaps <- PrePost_Phi %>% dplyr::select(
    CSI_Cutoff, Era, Salience_Group, N_Cases, Mean_Phi, Mean_Phi_Normalized,
    Strict_Split_Rate) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Salience_Group, values_from = c(
      N_Cases, Mean_Phi, Mean_Phi_Normalized, Strict_Split_Rate)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_High - Mean_Phi_Low,
    
    Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_High - Mean_Phi_Normalized_Low,
    
    Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_High - Strict_Split_Rate_Low) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    CSI_Cutoff, Era, Phi_Gap, Phi_Normalized_Gap, Strict_Split_Gap) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Era,
    values_from = c(Phi_Gap, Phi_Normalized_Gap, Strict_Split_Gap)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    Change_Phi_Gap = Phi_Gap_Post2010 - Phi_Gap_Pre2010,
    
    Change_Phi_Normalized_Gap = Phi_Normalized_Gap_Post2010 -
      Phi_Normalized_Gap_Pre2010,
    
    Change_Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Gap_Post2010 -
      Strict_Split_Gap_Pre2010)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication table: underlying high- and lower-salience estimates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PrePost_Phi_Table <- PrePost_Phi %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Cutoff = paste0("CSI >= ", CSI_Cutoff),
    
    Period =
      dplyr::recode(Era, Pre2010 = "Pre-2010", Post2010 = "Post-2010"),
    
    Group = dplyr::if_else(
        Salience_Group == "High", paste0("CSI >= ", CSI_Cutoff),
        paste0("CSI < ", CSI_Cutoff))) %>% dplyr::transmute(
    
    Cutoff,
    
    Period,
    
    Group,
    
    Cases = N_Cases,
    
    `Mean |phi|` = round(Mean_Phi, 3),
    
    `Normalized |phi|` = round(Mean_Phi_Normalized, 3),
    
    `Strict split` = scales::percent(Strict_Split_Rate, accuracy = 0.1))

knitr::kable(
  PrePost_Phi_Table, caption =
    "Appointing-party alignment before and after OT2010", booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))

PrePost_Gaps_Table <- PrePost_Gaps %>% dplyr::select(
    CSI_Cutoff, Phi_Gap_Pre2010, Phi_Gap_Post2010, Change_Phi_Gap,
    Phi_Normalized_Gap_Pre2010, Phi_Normalized_Gap_Post2010,
    Change_Phi_Normalized_Gap, Strict_Split_Gap_Pre2010,
    Strict_Split_Gap_Post2010, Change_Strict_Split_Gap) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -CSI_Cutoff, names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "Value") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    Measure = dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(
          Statistic, "Phi_Normalized") ~ "Normalized |phi| gap",
        
        stringr::str_detect(
          Statistic, "Strict_Split") ~ "Strict-split gap",
        
        TRUE ~ "Mean |phi| gap"),
    
    Period = dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(Statistic, "Pre2010") ~ "Pre-2010",
        
        stringr::str_detect(Statistic, "Post2010") ~ "Post-2010",
        
        stringr::str_detect(Statistic, "^Change") ~ "Change")) %>%
  dplyr::select(CSI_Cutoff, Measure, Period, Value) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Period, values_from = Value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    Cutoff = paste0("CSI >= ", CSI_Cutoff),
    
    Measure = factor(
        Measure, levels = c(
          "Mean |phi| gap", "Normalized |phi| gap", "Strict-split gap"))
) %>% dplyr::arrange(CSI_Cutoff, Measure) %>% dplyr::transmute(
    
    Cutoff,
    
    Measure = as.character(Measure),
    
    `Pre-2010` = round(`Pre-2010`, 3),
    
    `Post-2010` = round(`Post-2010`, 3),
    
    Change = round(Change, 3))

knitr::kable(
  PrePost_Gaps_Table, caption =
    "Change in the high-minus-low salience gap after OT2010", booktabs =
    TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

## Estimated Breakpoint in the Salience–Alignment Relationship

### Purpose

The following code estimates the Supreme Court term at which the relationship between case salience and appointing-party alignment changes most sharply.

The breakpoint search is conducted on the underlying contested-case data rather than on the five-term rolling series. This avoids using overlapping rolling windows to determine the timing of the change.

For every candidate breakpoint from OT1990 through OT2018, the analysis estimates the relationship between continuous CSI and appointing-party alignment before and after the candidate term while absorbing term-specific differences in the overall level of alignment. The selected breakpoint is the term producing the lowest residual sum of squares.

The principal search uses raw absolute phi. The procedure is repeated independently using margin-normalized phi as a robustness check.

Uncertainty in the location of the breakpoint is estimated using a **term-cluster bootstrap**. Supreme Court terms rather than individual cases are resampled, preserving the within-term dependence structure of the data. The resulting bootstrap distribution provides a 95% interval for the estimated breakpoint.

This data-driven breakpoint is distinct from the theoretically motivated OT2010 division used in the preceding descriptive table. The data-driven estimate can then be compared with the pre-specified OT2010 division.

### Created objects

- **break_candidates** — candidate breakpoint terms searched by the procedure.

- **Breakpoint_Data_Raw** — within-term transformed case-level data for raw absolute phi.

- **Breakpoint_Data_Normalized** — corresponding data for margin-normalized phi.

- **Breakpoint_Search_Raw** — raw-phi breakpoint search results for every candidate term.

- **Breakpoint_Search_Normalized** — normalized-phi breakpoint search results.

- **Breakpoint_Bootstrap** — term-cluster bootstrap distribution of estimated breakpoint terms.

- **Breakpoint_Summary** — point estimates, bootstrap intervals, and pre-/post-break CSI slopes.

- **Breakpoint_Table** — publication-facing summary table with reader-friendly column names.

```{r estimated-breakpoint}

# --- Estimated breakpoint in the salience-alignment relationship -------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Breakpoint-search parameters
#
# The candidate range is intentionally broader than OT2010 so that the
# data-driven search is not mechanically constrained to reproduce the
# theoretically motivated breakpoint.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

break_search_start <- 1990L

break_search_end <- 2018L

break_candidates <- seq.int(break_search_start, break_search_end)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Number of term-cluster bootstrap replications
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

break_boot_reps <- 1000L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare data for breakpoint estimation
#
# The transformation below removes the mean of both CSI and the outcome
# separately within each Supreme Court term.
#
# This is algebraically equivalent to including a fixed effect for every
# Supreme Court term in the breakpoint regression.
#
# The resulting breakpoint therefore concerns a change in the relationship
# between salience and appointing-party alignment rather than merely a change
# in the overall level of Court polarization over time.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

prepare_breakpoint_data <- function(
    data, outcome) {
  
  data %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(term), !is.na(csi), !is.na(.data[[outcome]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(term) %>% dplyr::mutate(
      
      CSI_Within = csi - mean(csi, na.rm = TRUE),
      
      Outcome_Within = .data[[outcome]] -
        mean(.data[[outcome]], na.rm = TRUE)) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(CSI_Within), is.finite(Outcome_Within))
}

Breakpoint_Data_Raw <- prepare_breakpoint_data(
  SCOTUS_Contested, "phi_abs")

Breakpoint_Data_Normalized <- prepare_breakpoint_data(
  SCOTUS_Contested, "phi_normalized")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Restrict raw and normalized analyses to the same set of Supreme Court terms
#
# This keeps the timing comparison between the two outcome measures directly
# comparable.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

common_break_terms <- intersect(
  unique(Breakpoint_Data_Raw$term),
  unique(Breakpoint_Data_Normalized$term)) %>% sort()

Breakpoint_Data_Raw <- Breakpoint_Data_Raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(term %in% common_break_terms)

Breakpoint_Data_Normalized <- Breakpoint_Data_Normalized %>%
  dplyr::filter(term %in% common_break_terms)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Breakpoint-search function
#
# For every candidate term b:
#
#   Pre-break CSI slope
#       = relationship between CSI and alignment before b
#
#   Slope change
#       = change in the CSI relationship beginning in b
#
#   Post-break CSI slope
#       = pre-break slope + slope change
#
# The best breakpoint is the candidate producing the smallest residual
# sum of squares.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

search_breakpoint <- function(
    data, candidates, weights = NULL) {
  
  if (
    is.null(weights)) {
    
    weights <- rep(1, nrow(data))
  }
  
  search_results <- purrr::map_dfr(
    candidates, function(b) {
      
      d <- data %>% dplyr::mutate(
          
          Post_Break = as.integer(term >= b),
          
          CSI_Post = CSI_Within * Post_Break)
      
      fit <- stats::lm(
        Outcome_Within ~ 0 + CSI_Within + CSI_Post, data = d, weights =
          weights)
      
      coefficients <- stats::coef(fit)
      
      pre_slope <- unname(coefficients["CSI_Within"])
      
      slope_change <- unname(coefficients["CSI_Post"])
      
      post_slope <- pre_slope + slope_change
      
      rss <- sum(weights * stats::residuals(fit)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
      
      tibble::tibble(
        
        Break_Term = b,
        
        RSS = rss,
        
        Pre_CSI_Slope = pre_slope,
        
        Slope_Change = slope_change,
        
        Post_CSI_Slope = post_slope)
    })
  
  search_results %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Delta_RSS = RSS - min(RSS, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Break_Term)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Primary breakpoint searches
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Search_Raw <- search_breakpoint(
  Breakpoint_Data_Raw, break_candidates)

Breakpoint_Search_Normalized <- search_breakpoint(
  Breakpoint_Data_Normalized, break_candidates)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify the best-fitting breakpoint
#
# If two candidates were ever exactly tied, the earlier term would be
# selected. Exact ties are unlikely in practice.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Best_Raw <- Breakpoint_Search_Raw %>%
  dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1)

Breakpoint_Best_Normalized <- Breakpoint_Search_Normalized %>%
  dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Term-cluster bootstrap
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(20260908)

Breakpoint_Bootstrap <- purrr::map_dfr(
  seq_len(break_boot_reps), function(r) {
    
    sampled_terms <- sample(
      common_break_terms, size = length(common_break_terms), replace =
        TRUE)
    
    term_frequency <- table(
      factor(sampled_terms, levels = common_break_terms))
    
    term_weights <- stats::setNames(
      as.numeric(term_frequency), as.character(common_break_terms))
    
    raw_weights <- unname(
      term_weights[
        as.character(Breakpoint_Data_Raw$term)])
    
    normalized_weights <- unname(
      term_weights[
        as.character(Breakpoint_Data_Normalized$term)])
    
    raw_search <- search_breakpoint(
      Breakpoint_Data_Raw, break_candidates, weights = raw_weights)
    
    normalized_search <- search_breakpoint(
      Breakpoint_Data_Normalized, break_candidates, weights =
        normalized_weights)
    
    raw_break <- raw_search %>% dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1) %>% dplyr::pull(Break_Term)
    
    normalized_break <- normalized_search %>%
      dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::pull(Break_Term)
    
    tibble::tibble(
      
      Replicate = r,
      
      Raw_Break = raw_break,
      
      Normalized_Break = normalized_break)
  })

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper for discrete bootstrap confidence intervals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

breakpoint_interval <- function(
    x) {
  
  c(
    Lower = as.integer(
        stats::quantile(x, probs = 0.025, type = 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    Median = as.integer(stats::median(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    Upper = as.integer(
        stats::quantile(x, probs = 0.975, type = 1, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

raw_break_interval <- breakpoint_interval(Breakpoint_Bootstrap$Raw_Break)

normalized_break_interval <- breakpoint_interval(
  Breakpoint_Bootstrap$Normalized_Break)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Summarize breakpoint estimates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  tibble::tibble(
    
    Measure = "Mean absolute phi",
    
    Estimated_Break = Breakpoint_Best_Raw$Break_Term,
    
    Bootstrap_Median = raw_break_interval[
        "Median"],
    
    CI_Lower = raw_break_interval[
        "Lower"],
    
    CI_Upper = raw_break_interval[
        "Upper"],
    
    Pre_CSI_Slope = Breakpoint_Best_Raw$Pre_CSI_Slope,
    
    Post_CSI_Slope = Breakpoint_Best_Raw$Post_CSI_Slope,
    
    Slope_Change = Breakpoint_Best_Raw$Slope_Change),
  
  tibble::tibble(
    
    Measure = "Margin-normalized phi",
    
    Estimated_Break = Breakpoint_Best_Normalized$Break_Term,
    
    Bootstrap_Median = normalized_break_interval[
        "Median"],
    
    CI_Lower = normalized_break_interval[
        "Lower"],
    
    CI_Upper = normalized_break_interval[
        "Upper"],
    
    Pre_CSI_Slope = Breakpoint_Best_Normalized$Pre_CSI_Slope,
    
    Post_CSI_Slope = Breakpoint_Best_Normalized$Post_CSI_Slope,
    
    Slope_Change = Breakpoint_Best_Normalized$Slope_Change))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication-facing breakpoint table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Table <- Breakpoint_Summary %>% dplyr::transmute(
    
    Measure,
    
    `Estimated break` = paste0("OT", Estimated_Break),
    
    `Bootstrap median` = paste0("OT", Bootstrap_Median),
    
    `95% bootstrap interval` = paste0("OT", CI_Lower, "-OT", CI_Upper),
    
    `Pre-break CSI slope` = round(Pre_CSI_Slope, 3),
    
    `Post-break CSI slope` = round(Post_CSI_Slope, 3),
    
    `Slope change` = round(Slope_Change, 3))

knitr::kable(
  Breakpoint_Table, caption =
    paste0(
      "Estimated breakpoint in the relationship between case salience ",
      "and appointing-party alignment"
),
  booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Five best-fitting candidate terms
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_TopCandidates <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  Breakpoint_Search_Raw %>% dplyr::arrange(RSS) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 5) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Mean absolute phi"),
  
  Breakpoint_Search_Normalized %>% dplyr::arrange(RSS) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 5) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Margin-normalized phi")) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Measure,
    
    Term = paste0("OT", Break_Term),
    
    `Difference from minimum RSS` = round(Delta_RSS, 4))

knitr::kable(
  Breakpoint_TopCandidates, caption =
    "Best-fitting candidate breakpoint terms", booktabs = TRUE)
```

# Salience Gap by Natural Court

### Purpose

The following code determines whether changes in the relationship between salience and appointing-party alignment coincide with changes in Supreme Court membership.

The analysis uses the same salience-band structure as the rolling salience-gap analysis. Cases with **CSI \< 2** form the common low-salience reference group, while higher-salience cases are divided into **CSI 2–4**, **CSI 5–6**, and **CSI \>= 7**.

For every Natural Court, the code calculates the difference between each higher-salience band and the CSI \< 2 reference group in:

- raw absolute phi;

- margin-normalized phi;

- strict appointing-party split rate.

Raw and margin-normalized phi are displayed in vertically stacked panels. Estimates are displayed only when both the reference and comparison groups contain at least five contested cases. The underlying estimates are retained regardless of sample size.

Natural Courts make it possible to compare the emerging salience gap with changes in Court membership.

### Created objects

- **NaturalCourt_Salience** — appointing-party alignment statistics by Natural Court and salience band.

- **NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps** — differences from the CSI \< 2 reference group by Natural Court.

- **NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Long** — long-format raw and normalized gap data used for plotting.

- **NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Table** — reader-facing Natural Court gap table retained for possible appendix use but not automatically printed.

- **p_natural_court_gaps** — vertically faceted figure showing raw and normalized salience gaps across successive Natural Courts.

```{r natural-court-salience-gaps}
#| fig-width: 6.27
#| fig-height: 6.8
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "100%"

# --- Salience gap by Natural Court -------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Salience bands
#
# CSI < 2 is the common low-salience reference.
#
#   CSI < 2
#   CSI 2-4
#   CSI 5-6
#   CSI >= 7
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

salience_band_levels <- c("CSI < 2", "CSI 2-4", "CSI 5-6", "CSI >= 7")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimum number of cases required to display a Natural Court comparison
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

min_cases_natural_court <- 5L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Alignment statistics by Natural Court and salience band
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NaturalCourt_Salience <- SCOTUS_Contested %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(naturalCourt)) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Salience_Band = dplyr::case_when(
        csi < 2                    ~ "CSI < 2",
        csi >= 2 & csi < 5         ~ "CSI 2-4",
        csi >= 5 & csi < 7         ~ "CSI 5-6",
        csi >= 7                   ~ "CSI >= 7",
        TRUE                       ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Salience_Band)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(naturalCourt, Salience_Band) %>% dplyr::summarise(
    
    N_Cases = dplyr::n(),
    
    Mean_Phi = safe_mean(phi_abs),
    
    Mean_Phi_Normalized = safe_mean(phi_normalized),
    
    Strict_Split_Rate = safe_rate(strict_party_split),
    
    .groups = "drop") %>% tidyr::complete(
    naturalCourt, Salience_Band = salience_band_levels, fill =
      list(N_Cases = 0L))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convert salience-band estimates to wide form
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NaturalCourt_Salience_Wide <- NaturalCourt_Salience %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Band_ID = dplyr::case_when(
        Salience_Band == "CSI < 2"  ~ "lt2",
        Salience_Band == "CSI 2-4"  ~ "b24",
        Salience_Band == "CSI 5-6"  ~ "b56",
        Salience_Band == "CSI >= 7" ~ "ge7",
        TRUE                        ~ NA_character_)) %>% dplyr::select(
    naturalCourt, Band_ID, N_Cases, Mean_Phi, Mean_Phi_Normalized,
    Strict_Split_Rate) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Band_ID, values_from = c(
      N_Cases, Mean_Phi, Mean_Phi_Normalized, Strict_Split_Rate))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate differences from the CSI < 2 reference group
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  NaturalCourt_Salience_Wide %>% dplyr::transmute(
      
      naturalCourt,
      
      Series = "CSI 2-4",
      
      N_Cases_Reference = N_Cases_lt2,
      
      N_Cases_Comparison = N_Cases_b24,
      
      Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases_lt2 >= min_cases_natural_court &
        N_Cases_b24 >= min_cases_natural_court,
      
      Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_b24 - Mean_Phi_lt2,
      
      Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_b24 -
        Mean_Phi_Normalized_lt2,
      
      Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_b24 - Strict_Split_Rate_lt2),
  
  NaturalCourt_Salience_Wide %>% dplyr::transmute(
      
      naturalCourt,
      
      Series = "CSI 5-6",
      
      N_Cases_Reference = N_Cases_lt2,
      
      N_Cases_Comparison = N_Cases_b56,
      
      Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases_lt2 >= min_cases_natural_court &
        N_Cases_b56 >= min_cases_natural_court,
      
      Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_b56 - Mean_Phi_lt2,
      
      Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_b56 -
        Mean_Phi_Normalized_lt2,
      
      Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_b56 - Strict_Split_Rate_lt2),
  
  # CSI >= 7 relative to CSI < 2
  NaturalCourt_Salience_Wide %>% dplyr::transmute(
      
      naturalCourt,
      
      Series = "CSI >= 7",
      
      N_Cases_Reference = N_Cases_lt2,
      
      N_Cases_Comparison = N_Cases_ge7,
      
      Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases_lt2 >= min_cases_natural_court &
        N_Cases_ge7 >= min_cases_natural_court,
      
      Phi_Gap = Mean_Phi_ge7 - Mean_Phi_lt2,
      
      Phi_Normalized_Gap = Mean_Phi_Normalized_ge7 -
        Mean_Phi_Normalized_lt2,
      
      Strict_Split_Gap = Strict_Split_Rate_ge7 - Strict_Split_Rate_lt2)
) %>% dplyr::left_join(
    NaturalCourt_Descriptives %>% dplyr::select(
        naturalCourt, Court_Index, Court_Period, Chief, R_Appointed,
        D_Appointed), by = "naturalCourt") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Court_Index, Series)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reader-facing Natural Court table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Table <- NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Period = Court_Period,
    
    Chief,
    
    Band = Series,
    
    `Reference cases` = N_Cases_Reference,
    
    `Comparison cases` = N_Cases_Comparison,
    
    `Mean |phi| gap` = round(Phi_Gap, 3),
    
    `Normalized |phi| gap` = round(Phi_Normalized_Gap, 3),
    
    `Strict-split gap` = scales::percent(Strict_Split_Gap, accuracy = 0.1)
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reshape raw and normalized phi gaps for plotting
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Long <- NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps %>%
  dplyr::select(
    naturalCourt, Court_Index, Court_Period, Series, N_Cases_Reference,
    N_Cases_Comparison, Eligible_For_Plot, Phi_Gap, Phi_Normalized_Gap) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Phi_Gap, Phi_Normalized_Gap), names_to = "Gap_Measure",
    values_to = "Gap_Value") %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Gap_Measure = dplyr::recode(
        Gap_Measure, Phi_Gap = "Mean absolute phi gap", Phi_Normalized_Gap =
          "Mean margin-normalized phi gap"),
    
    Gap_Measure = factor(
        Gap_Measure, levels = c(
          "Mean absolute phi gap", "Mean margin-normalized phi gap")),
    
    Series =
      factor(Series, levels = c("CSI 2-4", "CSI 5-6", "CSI >= 7")),
    
    Gap_Value_Plot = dplyr::if_else(
        Eligible_For_Plot & !is.na(Gap_Value), Gap_Value, NA_real_)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Gap_Measure, Series) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Court_Index, .by_group = TRUE) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Gap_Available = !is.na(Gap_Value_Plot),
    
    Plot_Run = cumsum(
        Gap_Available != dplyr::lag(
            Gap_Available, default = dplyr::first(Gap_Available)))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Natural Court axis labels
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

NaturalCourt_Axis <- NaturalCourt_Descriptives %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Court_Index) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Court_Index, Court_Period)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

natural_court_gap_colors <- c(
  "CSI 2-4"  = "#B8C95A", "CSI 5-6"  = "#E9962F", "CSI >= 7" = "#9E0142")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Natural Court salience-gap figure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_natural_court_gaps <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.30) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Long, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Court_Index, y = Gap_Value_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE)), color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.05, alpha = 0.90, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Long, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Court_Index, y = Gap_Value_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE), color = Series),
    linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 0.97, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = NaturalCourt_Salience_Gaps_Long,
    ggplot2::aes(x = Court_Index, y = Gap_Value_Plot, color = Series),
    size = 1.5, alpha = 0.97, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Gap_Measure, ncol = 1) +
  
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = natural_court_gap_colors,
    breaks = c("CSI 2-4", "CSI 5-6", "CSI >= 7"), name = NULL) +
  
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = NaturalCourt_Axis$Court_Index, labels =
      NaturalCourt_Axis$Court_Period, expand =
      ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))) +
  
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Salience gaps across Supreme Court compositions", x = NULL, y =
      "Difference from CSI < 2 in phi coefficient") +
  
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  
  ggplot2::theme(
    
    legend.position = "bottom",
    
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines"),
    
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    axis.text.x =
      ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 7),
    
    axis.title.y =
      ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 10)),
    
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5))

print(p_natural_court_gaps)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    fig_dir, "03_phi_salience_gap_by_natural_court.emf"), plot =
    p_natural_court_gaps, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height = 6.8,
  units = "in")
```

# Strict Appointing-Party Split Proportions

### Purpose

The following code provides an intuitive binary complement to the continuous phi measures by showing the proportion of salient contested cases producing a **strict appointing-party split**.

A strict split occurs when all participating Republican-appointed justices fall on one disposition side and all participating Democratic-appointed justices fall on the other.

Unlike the salience-gap figures, this analysis retains the principal **nested CSI thresholds from 3 through 7**. The question here is not how one salience band differs from a common low-salience reference, but rather:

*Among contested cases at least this salient, what proportion produce a complete appointing-party split?*

The rolling statistic uses the same trailing windows as the other historical figures. Estimates based on fewer than five contested cases are suppressed for plotting only.

A diagnostic observation is retained for the rolling window ending in OT2024. That window contains OT2020–OT2024 and should reproduce the previously observed **20 strict splits among 32 CSI \>= 5 contested cases, or 62.5%**, if the final merged data reproduce the exploratory result.

### Created objects

- **Rolling_Strict_Thresholds** — plotting dataset containing trailing strict-split proportions for CSI thresholds 3–7.

- **p_strict_thresholds** — unshaded rolling strict-split figure.

- **p_strict_thresholds_shaded** — corresponding figure with Natural Court composition shading.

- **Modern_Strict_Split_Check** — diagnostic observation for CSI \>= 5 during OT2020–OT2024.

- **Modern_Strict_Split_Check_Table** — reader-facing version of that diagnostic.

```{r rolling-strict-party-splits}
#| fig-width: 6.27
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "100%"

# --- Strict appointing-party split proportions -------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimum sample size for displayed rolling estimates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

min_cases_strict_plot <- 5L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Principal CSI thresholds
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

strict_series_levels <- paste0("CSI >= ", csi_cutoffs)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare rolling strict-split plotting data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rolling_Strict_Thresholds <- Rolling_Phi_Thresholds %>%
  dplyr::filter(CSI_Cutoff %in% csi_cutoffs) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Series = paste0("CSI >= ", CSI_Cutoff),
    
    Series = factor(Series, levels = strict_series_levels),
    
    Eligible_For_Plot = N_Cases >= min_cases_strict_plot &
      !is.na(Strict_Split_Rate),
    
    Strict_Split_Rate_Plot =
      dplyr::if_else(Eligible_For_Plot, Strict_Split_Rate, NA_real_)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Series) %>% dplyr::arrange(Year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    Plot_Available = !is.na(Strict_Split_Rate_Plot),
    
    Plot_Run = cumsum(
        Plot_Available != dplyr::lag(
            Plot_Available, default = dplyr::first(Plot_Available)))
) %>% dplyr::ungroup()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strict-split colors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

strict_plot_colors <- c(
  "CSI >= 3" = "#B8C95A", "CSI >= 4" = "#D9B43B", "CSI >= 5" = "#E9962F",
  "CSI >= 6" = "#E85B3A", "CSI >= 7" = "#9E0142")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared scales and theme
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

strict_split_scales <- list(
  
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = strict_plot_colors, breaks = strict_series_levels, labels =
      strict_series_levels, name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
  
  ggplot2::guides(
    color = ggplot2::guide_legend(
        nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE, override.aes =
          list(linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 1))),
  
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(analysis_start_term, analysis_end_term),
    breaks = seq(1960, 2020, by = 10), expand =
      ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0))),
  
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2), labels =
      scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand =
      ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))),
  
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Strict appointing-party splits in salient contested cases", x =
      "Year", y = "Strict appointing-party split rate"),
  
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(),
  
  ggplot2::theme(
    
    legend.position = "bottom",
    
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    axis.title.x =
      ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 10)),
    
    axis.title.y =
      ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 10)),
    
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Figure without Natural Court shading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_strict_thresholds <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  
  # White underlay.
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Strict_Thresholds, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Strict_Split_Rate_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE)), color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.05, alpha = 0.90, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  # Strict-split trajectories.
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Strict_Thresholds, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Strict_Split_Rate_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE), color = Series),
    linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 0.97, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  strict_split_scales

print(p_strict_thresholds)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    fig_dir, "04_strict_party_split_rolling_thresholds.emf"), plot =
    p_strict_thresholds, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height = 4.2,
  units = "in")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. Figure with Natural Court composition shading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_strict_thresholds_shaded <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  
  ggplot2::geom_rect(
    data = NaturalCourt_Shading, ggplot2::aes(
      xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill =
        Shade_Colour, alpha = Shade_Intensity), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  ggplot2::scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
  
  ggplot2::scale_alpha_identity(guide = "none") +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Strict_Thresholds, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Strict_Split_Rate_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE)), color = "white",
    linewidth = 1.05, alpha = 0.90, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = Rolling_Strict_Thresholds, ggplot2::aes(
      x = Year, y = Strict_Split_Rate_Plot, group =
        interaction(Series, Plot_Run, drop = TRUE), color = Series),
    linewidth = 0.62, alpha = 0.97, na.rm = TRUE) +
  
  strict_split_scales

print(p_strict_thresholds_shaded)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    fig_dir, "04_strict_party_split_rolling_thresholds_shaded.emf"), plot =
    p_strict_thresholds_shaded, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height =
    4.2, units = "in")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostic check corresponding to OT2020-OT2024
#
# Under the current trailing-window definition, Year = 2024 represents:
#
# OT2020, OT2021, OT2022, OT2023, OT2024.
#
# This replaces the earlier centered-window check at Center_Term = 2022.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Modern_Strict_Split_Check <- Rolling_Phi_Thresholds %>%
  dplyr::filter(Year == 2024, CSI_Cutoff == 5) %>% dplyr::select(
    Year, Window_Start, Window_End, CSI_Cutoff, N_Cases, Strict_Split_N,
    Strict_Split_Rate)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reader-facing diagnostic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Modern_Strict_Split_Check_Table <- Modern_Strict_Split_Check %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Window = paste0("OT", Window_Start, "-OT", Window_End),
    
    `CSI threshold` = paste0("CSI >= ", CSI_Cutoff),
    
    Cases = N_Cases,
    
    `Strict splits` = Strict_Split_N,
    
    `Strict-split rate` =
      scales::percent(Strict_Split_Rate, accuracy = 0.1))

knitr::kable(
  Modern_Strict_Split_Check_Table, caption =
    paste0(
      "Diagnostic strict-split rate for CSI >= 5 contested cases ",
      "during OT2020-OT2024"
),
  booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

# Predictive Analysis of the Salience–Alignment Relationship

## Vote Division by Case Salience

### Purpose

The following code examines whether case salience is associated with the **propensity for substantial disagreement in the first place**, before restricting the analysis to contested cases.

Unlike the subsequent phi analyses, this section uses the complete merged CSI case universe, `SCOTUS_CaseData`. Cases are classified according to whether the decision was unanimous, contained exactly one minority vote, contained at least two minority votes, or was closely divided with at least three minority votes.

To remain consistent with the descriptive salience-gap analysis, cases are grouped into **CSI \< 2**, **CSI 2–4**, **CSI 5–6**, and **CSI \>= 7**. The contested and closely divided categories are intentionally nested: closely divided cases form a subset of cases with at least two minority votes.

This distinguishes two outcomes: One, whether salience is associated with substantial disagreement, and two, among contested cases, whether that disagreement is aligned by appointing-president party.

### Created objects

- **Vote_Division_Data** — complete CSI case universe with salience-band and vote-division indicators.

- **Vote_Division_By_Salience** — descriptive vote-division rates by salience band.

- **Vote_Division_Table** — publication-facing table of vote-division patterns.

```{r vote-division-by-salience}

# --- Vote division by case salience ------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Salience bands
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

vote_division_salience_levels <- c(
  "CSI < 2", "CSI 2-4", "CSI 5-6", "CSI >= 7")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Full case universe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Vote_Division_Data <- SCOTUS_CaseData %>% dplyr::filter(
    term >= analysis_start_term, term <= analysis_end_term, !is.na(csi),
    !is.na(minVotes)) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Salience_Band = dplyr::case_when(
        csi < 2                    ~ "CSI < 2",
        csi >= 2 & csi < 5        ~ "CSI 2-4",
        csi >= 5 & csi < 7        ~ "CSI 5-6",
        csi >= 7                   ~ "CSI >= 7",
        TRUE                       ~ NA_character_),
    
    Salience_Band =
      factor(Salience_Band, levels = vote_division_salience_levels),
    
    Unanimous = minVotes == 0,
    
    One_Minority_Vote = minVotes == 1,
    
    Contested = minVotes >= 2,
    
    Closely_Divided = minVotes >= 3) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Salience_Band))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Descriptive vote-division statistics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Vote_Division_By_Salience <- Vote_Division_Data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Salience_Band) %>% dplyr::summarise(
    
    N_Cases = dplyr::n(),
    
    Unanimous_Rate = safe_rate(Unanimous),
    
    One_Minority_Rate = safe_rate(One_Minority_Vote),
    
    Contested_Rate = safe_rate(Contested),
    
    Closely_Divided_Rate = safe_rate(Closely_Divided),
    
    .groups = "drop")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication-facing table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Vote_Division_Table <- Vote_Division_By_Salience %>% dplyr::transmute(
    
    `CSI band` = as.character(Salience_Band),
    
    Cases = N_Cases,
    
    Unanimous = scales::percent(Unanimous_Rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    
    `One minority vote` =
      scales::percent(One_Minority_Rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    
    `Contested (2+ minority votes)` =
      scales::percent(Contested_Rate, accuracy = 0.1),
    
    `Closely divided (3+ minority votes)` =
      scales::percent(Closely_Divided_Rate, accuracy = 0.1))

knitr::kable(
  Vote_Division_Table, caption = "Vote division by case salience",
  booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

## CSI Regression Model

### Purpose

Estimate whether case salience is associated with the probability that a Supreme Court case is contested. A contested case is defined as a case with at least two minority votes.

The model uses CSI as a continuous predictor, includes October Term fixed effects, and clusters standard errors by October Term.

### Created objects

- `Contested_Model_Data` — data used in the CSI regression model, including the binary contested-case indicator.

- `Contested_CSI_Model` — regression of contested-case status on CSI with October Term fixed effects.

- `Contested_CSI_VCov` — term-clustered variance-covariance matrix.

- `Contested_CSI_Result` — regression results with clustered standard errors.

- `Contested_CSI_Estimate` — estimated CSI coefficient.

- `Contested_CSI_SE` — clustered standard error for the CSI coefficient.

- `Contested_CSI_P` — p-value for the CSI coefficient.

- `Contested_CSI_Lower` and `Contested_CSI_Upper` — lower and upper bounds of the 95% confidence interval.

- `Contested_CSI_Table` — publication-facing regression table.

```{r contested-case-regressions}

# --- CSI regression models --------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regression dataset
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

contested_csi_period_levels <- c(
  "1955-1964",
  "1965-1974",
  "1975-1984",
  "1985-1994",
  "1995-2004",
  "2005-2009",
  "2010-2014",
  "2015-2019",
  "2020-2024"
)

Contested_CSI_Data <- SCOTUS_CaseData %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    term >= analysis_start_term,
    term <= analysis_end_term,
    !is.na(csi),
    !is.na(minVotes)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    contested_case = as.integer(minVotes >= 2),
    
    Regression_Period = dplyr::case_when(
      term >= 1955 & term <= 1964 ~ "1955-1964",
      term >= 1965 & term <= 1974 ~ "1965-1974",
      term >= 1975 & term <= 1984 ~ "1975-1984",
      term >= 1985 & term <= 1994 ~ "1985-1994",
      term >= 1995 & term <= 2004 ~ "1995-2004",
      term >= 2005 & term <= 2009 ~ "2005-2009",
      term >= 2010 & term <= 2014 ~ "2010-2014",
      term >= 2015 & term <= 2019 ~ "2015-2019",
      term >= 2020 & term <= 2024 ~ "2020-2024",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    Regression_Period = factor(
      Regression_Period,
      levels = contested_csi_period_levels
    )
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clustered-result helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_contested_csi <- function(
    model, vcov_matrix, data, period) {
  
  estimate <- stats::coef(model)[["csi"]]
  
  standard_error <- unname(
    sqrt(vcov_matrix["csi", "csi"])
  )
  
  n_terms <- dplyr::n_distinct(data$term)
  
  cluster_df <- n_terms - 1L
  
  critical_value <- stats::qt(
    0.975,
    df = cluster_df
  )
  
  t_value <- estimate / standard_error
  
  p_value <- 2 * stats::pt(
    abs(t_value),
    df = cluster_df,
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
  
  tibble::tibble(
    
    Period = period,
    
    Estimate = as.numeric(estimate),
    
    Clustered_SE = as.numeric(standard_error),
    
    CI_Lower = as.numeric(
      estimate - critical_value * standard_error
    ),
    
    CI_Upper = as.numeric(
      estimate + critical_value * standard_error
    ),
    
    P_Value = as.numeric(p_value),
    
    N_Cases = as.integer(stats::nobs(model)),
    
    N_Terms = as.integer(n_terms)
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Overall OT1953-OT2024 regression
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_contested_csi_all <- stats::lm(
  contested_case ~ csi + factor(term),
  data = Contested_CSI_Data
)

vcov_contested_csi_all <- sandwich::vcovCL(
  m_contested_csi_all,
  cluster = Contested_CSI_Data$term,
  type = "HC1"
)

Contested_CSI_Results_Overall <- extract_contested_csi(
  model = m_contested_csi_all,
  vcov_matrix = vcov_contested_csi_all,
  data = Contested_CSI_Data,
  period = "OT1953-OT2024"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. Separate regressions by historical period
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Contested_CSI_Period_Data <- Contested_CSI_Data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Regression_Period)
  ) %>%
  split(
    .$Regression_Period
  )

m_contested_csi_periods <- purrr::map(
  Contested_CSI_Period_Data,
  function(data_i) {
    
    stats::lm(
      contested_case ~ csi + factor(term),
      data = data_i
    )
  }
)

vcov_contested_csi_periods <- purrr::map2(
  m_contested_csi_periods,
  Contested_CSI_Period_Data,
  function(model_i, data_i) {
    
    sandwich::vcovCL(
      model_i,
      cluster = data_i$term,
      type = "HC1"
    )
  }
)

Contested_CSI_Results_By_Period <- purrr::map_dfr(
  names(m_contested_csi_periods),
  function(period_i) {
    
    extract_contested_csi(
      model = m_contested_csi_periods[[period_i]],
      vcov_matrix =
        vcov_contested_csi_periods[[period_i]],
      data = Contested_CSI_Period_Data[[period_i]],
      period = period_i
    )
  }
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine overall and period-specific results
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Contested_CSI_Results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  Contested_CSI_Results_Overall,
  Contested_CSI_Results_By_Period
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication-facing regression table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Contested_CSI_Table <- Contested_CSI_Results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    `95% CI` = sprintf(
      "%.3f to %.3f",
      CI_Lower,
      CI_Upper
    ),
    
    `p value` = dplyr::if_else(
      P_Value < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
      sprintf("%.3f", P_Value)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Period,
    
    Estimate = round(Estimate, 3),
    
    `Clustered SE` = round(Clustered_SE, 3),
    
    `95% CI`,
    
    `p value`,
    
    Cases = N_Cases,
    
    Terms = N_Terms
  )

knitr::kable(
  Contested_CSI_Table,
  caption =
    "Case salience and the probability of a contested Supreme Court decision",
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

## Breakpoint Diagnostics

### Purpose

The following code evaluates how sharply the previously estimated breakpoint in the salience–alignment relationship is identified.

First, the candidate breakpoint range is widened from OT1990–OT2018 to **OT1980–OT2018**.The wider range checks whether the earlier normalized-phi interval was constrained by the OT1990 lower bound.

The code then plots the complete residual-sum-of-squares profile across candidate terms. A narrow RSS minimum indicates a more precisely located breakpoint; a flatter profile indicates greater timing uncertainty.

A second term-cluster bootstrap is conducted using the wider candidate range. The frequency with which each candidate term is selected is displayed directly. The diagnostics show whether the breakpoint is concentrated around a narrow group of terms or is weakly identified.

### Created objects

- **break_candidates_wide** — widened OT1980–OT2018 breakpoint-search range.

- **Breakpoint_Search_Raw_Wide** — widened raw-phi breakpoint profile.

- **Breakpoint_Search_Normalized_Wide** — widened normalized-phi breakpoint profile.

- **Breakpoint_Best_Wide** — best-fitting widened breakpoint for each outcome.

- **Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Wide** — term-cluster bootstrap estimates using the widened search range.

- **Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Frequency** — frequency with which each candidate term is selected.

- **Breakpoint_Diagnostic_Summary** — publication-facing comparison of original and widened breakpoint estimates.

- **p_breakpoint_profile** — complete RSS-profile diagnostic.

- **p_breakpoint_bootstrap** — bootstrap breakpoint-frequency diagnostic.

```{r breakpoint-diagnostics}
#| fig-width: 6.27
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "100%"

# --- Breakpoint diagnostics --------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wider candidate range
#
# The original search used OT1990-OT2018.
#
# The widened search tests whether the normalized result was being constrained
# by the lower boundary of that range.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

break_candidates_wide <- seq.int(1980L, 2018L)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wider point-estimate searches
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Search_Raw_Wide <- search_breakpoint(
  Breakpoint_Data_Raw, break_candidates_wide)

Breakpoint_Search_Normalized_Wide <- search_breakpoint(
  Breakpoint_Data_Normalized, break_candidates_wide)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Best-fitting widened breakpoint
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Best_Raw_Wide <- Breakpoint_Search_Raw_Wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(RSS)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1)

Breakpoint_Best_Normalized_Wide <- Breakpoint_Search_Normalized_Wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(RSS)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1)

Breakpoint_Best_Wide <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  Breakpoint_Best_Raw_Wide %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Mean absolute phi"),
  
  Breakpoint_Best_Normalized_Wide %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Margin-normalized phi"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Complete RSS profiles
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Profile <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  Breakpoint_Search_Raw_Wide %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Mean absolute phi"),
  
  Breakpoint_Search_Normalized_Wide %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Margin-normalized phi")) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Measure = factor(
        Measure, levels = c("Mean absolute phi", "Margin-normalized phi")
))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RSS-profile figure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_breakpoint_profile <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  Breakpoint_Profile, ggplot2::aes(x = Break_Term, y = Delta_RSS)) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.70) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    data = Breakpoint_Best_Wide, ggplot2::aes(xintercept = Break_Term),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.45) +
  
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Measure, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2015, by = 5)) +
  
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Breakpoint fit across candidate Supreme Court terms", x =
      "Candidate breakpoint term", y = "Difference from minimum RSS") +
  
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  
  ggplot2::theme(
    
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines"),
    
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

print(p_breakpoint_profile)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "05_breakpoint_rss_profile.emf"), plot =
    p_breakpoint_profile, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height = 6.2,
  units = "in")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wider term-cluster bootstrap
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

break_diag_boot_reps <- 1000L

set.seed(20260908)

Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Wide <- purrr::map_dfr(
  seq_len(break_diag_boot_reps), function(r) {
    
    sampled_terms <- sample(
      common_break_terms, size = length(common_break_terms), replace =
        TRUE)
    
    term_frequency <- table(
      factor(sampled_terms, levels = common_break_terms))
    
    term_weights <- stats::setNames(
      as.numeric(term_frequency), as.character(common_break_terms))
    
    raw_weights <- unname(
      term_weights[
        as.character(Breakpoint_Data_Raw$term)])
    
    normalized_weights <- unname(
      term_weights[
        as.character(Breakpoint_Data_Normalized$term)])
    
    raw_search <- search_breakpoint(
      Breakpoint_Data_Raw, break_candidates_wide, weights = raw_weights)
    
    normalized_search <- search_breakpoint(
      Breakpoint_Data_Normalized, break_candidates_wide, weights =
        normalized_weights)
    
    raw_break <- raw_search %>% dplyr::filter(is.finite(RSS)) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::pull(Break_Term)
    
    normalized_break <- normalized_search %>%
      dplyr::filter(is.finite(RSS)) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(RSS, Break_Term) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::pull(Break_Term)
    
    tibble::tibble(
      
      Replicate = r,
      
      Raw_Break = raw_break,
      
      Normalized_Break = normalized_break)
  })

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bootstrap selection frequencies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Frequency <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Wide %>%
    dplyr::count(Raw_Break, name = "Selections") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Break_Term = Raw_Break) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Mean absolute phi"),
  
  Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Wide %>%
    dplyr::count(Normalized_Break, name = "Selections") %>%
    dplyr::rename(Break_Term = Normalized_Break) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Measure = "Margin-normalized phi")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Measure) %>% tidyr::complete(
    Break_Term = break_candidates_wide, fill = list(Selections = 0L)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    Selection_Rate = Selections / sum(Selections),
    
    Measure = factor(
        Measure, levels = c("Mean absolute phi", "Margin-normalized phi")
)) %>% dplyr::ungroup()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bootstrap-frequency figure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

p_breakpoint_bootstrap <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Frequency,
  ggplot2::aes(x = Break_Term, y = Selection_Rate)) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
  
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.3) +
  
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Measure, ncol = 1) +
  
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2015, by = 5)) +
  
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Bootstrap distribution of estimated breakpoint terms", x =
      "Estimated breakpoint term", y = "Share of bootstrap samples") +
  
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  
  ggplot2::theme(
    
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines"),
    
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

print(p_breakpoint_bootstrap)

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    fig_dir, "06_breakpoint_bootstrap_distribution.emf"), plot =
    p_breakpoint_bootstrap, device = devEMF::emf, width = 6.27, height =
    6.2, units = "in")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostic summary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

raw_wide_interval <- breakpoint_interval(
  Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Wide$Raw_Break)

normalized_wide_interval <- breakpoint_interval(
  Breakpoint_Bootstrap_Wide$Normalized_Break)

Breakpoint_Diagnostic_Summary <- tibble::tibble(
  
  Measure = c("Mean absolute phi", "Margin-normalized phi"),
  
  Original_Break = c(
    Breakpoint_Best_Raw$Break_Term, Breakpoint_Best_Normalized$Break_Term),
  
  Wide_Break = c(
    Breakpoint_Best_Raw_Wide$Break_Term,
    Breakpoint_Best_Normalized_Wide$Break_Term),
  
  Bootstrap_Median = c(
    raw_wide_interval[
      "Median"], normalized_wide_interval[
      "Median"]),
  
  CI_Lower = c(
    raw_wide_interval[
      "Lower"], normalized_wide_interval[
      "Lower"]),
  
  CI_Upper = c(
    raw_wide_interval[
      "Upper"], normalized_wide_interval[
      "Upper"]))

Breakpoint_Diagnostic_Table <- Breakpoint_Diagnostic_Summary %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Measure,
    
    `Original search` = paste0("OT", Original_Break),
    
    `Wider search` = paste0("OT", Wide_Break),
    
    `Bootstrap median` = paste0("OT", Bootstrap_Median),
    
    `95% bootstrap interval` = paste0("OT", CI_Lower, "-OT", CI_Upper))

knitr::kable(
  Breakpoint_Diagnostic_Table, caption =
    "Breakpoint robustness to a wider candidate-term search", booktabs =
    TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "l"))
```

# Main Regression Models

### Purpose

The following code formally tests whether the relationship between continuous case salience and appointing-party alignment has changed over time.

The principal models use the contested-case sample and absorb **Supreme Court term fixed effects**. This is important because it removes term-specific changes in the overall level of appointing-party alignment. The interaction terms therefore test whether more-salient cases are differently aligned than less-salient cases within the same Supreme Court Term, rather than merely detecting that the Court as a whole became more polarized.

Two temporal specifications are estimated. The first allows the CSI slope to change linearly by decade across the full OT1953–OT2024 period. The second uses the theoretically motivated OT2010 division and estimates directly whether the CSI slope differs before and after OT2010.

Raw absolute phi is the principal outcome. Margin-normalized phi is estimated in parallel. Standard errors are clustered by Supreme Court term, and inference uses the number of term clusters rather than treating individual cases as independent temporal observations.

### Created objects

- **Model_Data** — contested-case regression sample.

- **m_phi_time** — raw-phi model allowing the CSI slope to change by decade.

- **m_phi_normalized_time** — corresponding normalized-phi model.

- **m_phi_post2010** — raw-phi pre-/post-2010 slope-change model.

- **m_phi_normalized_post2010** — corresponding normalized-phi model.

- **Inferential_Model_Results** — clustered coefficient and slope estimates.

- **Inferential_Model_Table** — publication-facing model summary.

```{r main-inferential-models}

# --- Main inferential models -------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regression dataset
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Model_Data <- SCOTUS_Contested %>% dplyr::filter(
    term >= analysis_start_term, term <= analysis_end_term, !is.na(csi),
    !is.na(phi_abs), !is.na(phi_normalized)) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Post2010 = as.integer(term >= 2010),
    
    Time_Decade = (term - analysis_start_term) / 10)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cluster-robust covariance helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cluster_vcov <- function(
    model, cluster) {
  
  sandwich::vcovCL(model, cluster = cluster, type = "HC1")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cluster-robust linear-combination helper
#
# This function allows direct calculation of:
#
#   - pre-period CSI slope;
#   - post-period CSI slope;
#   - change in CSI slope;
#   - change in the CSI slope per decade.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cluster_contrast <- function(
    model, vcov_matrix, weights, cluster_df, outcome, specification,
    quantity) {
  
  beta <- stats::coef(model)
  
  coefficient_names <- names(weights)
  
  estimate <- sum(weights * beta[coefficient_names])
  
  variance <- as.numeric(
      t(weights) %*%
        vcov_matrix[
          coefficient_names, coefficient_names, drop = FALSE] %*%
        weights)
  
  standard_error <- sqrt(variance)
  
  critical_value <- stats::qt(0.975, df = cluster_df)
  
  t_value <- estimate / standard_error
  
  p_value <- 2 *
    stats::pt(abs(t_value), df = cluster_df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    
    Outcome = outcome,
    
    Specification = specification,
    
    Quantity = quantity,
    
    Estimate = estimate,
    
    Clustered_SE = standard_error,
    
    CI_Lower = estimate - critical_value * standard_error,
    
    CI_Upper = estimate + critical_value * standard_error,
    
    P_Value = p_value)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Number of independent term clusters
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

n_term_clusters <- dplyr::n_distinct(Model_Data$term)

cluster_df <- n_term_clusters - 1L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Continuous historical change in the CSI slope
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_phi_time <- stats::lm(
  phi_abs ~ csi + csi:Time_Decade + factor(term), data = Model_Data)

vcov_phi_time <- cluster_vcov(m_phi_time, Model_Data$term)

m_phi_normalized_time <- stats::lm(
  phi_normalized ~ csi + csi:Time_Decade + factor(term), data = Model_Data)

vcov_phi_normalized_time <- cluster_vcov(
  m_phi_normalized_time, Model_Data$term)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. Theory-motivated OT2010 slope change
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_phi_post2010 <- stats::lm(
  phi_abs ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term), data = Model_Data)

vcov_phi_post2010 <- cluster_vcov(m_phi_post2010, Model_Data$term)

m_phi_normalized_post2010 <- stats::lm(
  phi_normalized ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term), data = Model_Data)

vcov_phi_normalized_post2010 <- cluster_vcov(
  m_phi_normalized_post2010, Model_Data$term)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract quantities of substantive interest
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Inferential_Model_Results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Raw phi: continuous historical change
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_time, vcov_matrix = vcov_phi_time, weights =
      c("csi:Time_Decade" = 1), cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome =
      "Mean absolute phi", specification = "Continuous time", quantity =
      "Change in CSI slope per decade"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normalized phi: continuous historical change
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_normalized_time, vcov_matrix = vcov_phi_normalized_time,
    weights = c("csi:Time_Decade" = 1), cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome =
      "Margin-normalized phi", specification = "Continuous time", quantity =
      "Change in CSI slope per decade"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Raw phi: pre-2010 slope
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_post2010, vcov_matrix = vcov_phi_post2010, weights =
      c("csi" = 1), cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome =
```
