```{r main-inferential-models}
      "Mean absolute phi", specification = "OT2010 break", quantity =
      "Pre-2010 CSI slope"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Raw phi: post-2010 slope
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_post2010, vcov_matrix = vcov_phi_post2010, weights =
      c("csi" = 1, "csi:Post2010" = 1), cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome =
      "Mean absolute phi", specification = "OT2010 break", quantity =
      "Post-2010 CSI slope"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Raw phi: slope change
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_post2010, vcov_matrix = vcov_phi_post2010, weights =
      c("csi:Post2010" = 1), cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome =
      "Mean absolute phi", specification = "OT2010 break", quantity =
      "Change in CSI slope"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normalized phi: pre-2010 slope
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_normalized_post2010, vcov_matrix =
      vcov_phi_normalized_post2010, weights = c("csi" = 1), cluster_df =
      cluster_df, outcome = "Margin-normalized phi", specification =
      "OT2010 break", quantity = "Pre-2010 CSI slope"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normalized phi: post-2010 slope
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_normalized_post2010, vcov_matrix =
      vcov_phi_normalized_post2010, weights =
      c("csi" = 1, "csi:Post2010" = 1), cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome =
      "Margin-normalized phi", specification = "OT2010 break", quantity =
      "Post-2010 CSI slope"),
  
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normalized phi: slope change
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = m_phi_normalized_post2010, vcov_matrix =
      vcov_phi_normalized_post2010, weights = c("csi:Post2010" = 1),
    cluster_df = cluster_df, outcome = "Margin-normalized phi",
    specification = "OT2010 break", quantity = "Change in CSI slope"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication-facing model table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Inferential_Model_Table <- Inferential_Model_Results %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    `95% CI` = paste0(
        sprintf("%.3f", CI_Lower), " to ", sprintf("%.3f", CI_Upper)),
    
    `p value` = dplyr::if_else(
        P_Value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", P_Value))) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Outcome,
    
    Specification,
    
    Quantity,
    
    Estimate = round(Estimate, 3),
    
    `Clustered SE` = round(Clustered_SE, 3),
    
    `95% CI`,
    
    `p value`)

knitr::kable(
  Inferential_Model_Table, caption =
    "Case salience and appointing-party alignment over time", booktabs =
    TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "l", "r"))
```

# Inferential Robustness Checks

### Purpose

The following code evaluates whether the principal inferential result depends on alternative modeling choices or sample definitions.

The robustness analysis first adds SCDB issue-area controls to determine whether the changing salience–alignment relationship can be explained by changes in the substantive composition of the Court's docket. It then estimates the OT2010 interaction using alternative definitions of a contested case: all non-unanimous cases, the principal two-or-more-minority-vote sample, and cases with at least three minority votes.

A further sensitivity model replaces OT2010 with the **data-driven breakpoint identified by the raw-phi breakpoint analysis**. Because this breakpoint was selected from the same data, its coefficient is treated as a sensitivity estimate rather than as an independent confirmatory test.

Fractional-logit models provide a nonlinear robustness check appropriate to outcomes bounded between zero and one. Finally, a linear-probability model applies the same continuous-salience specification to the intuitive binary strict appointing-party split outcome.

### Created objects

- **Robustness_Issue_Results** — OT2010 interaction estimates with issue-area controls.

- **Robustness_Sample_Results** — interaction estimates under alternative contested-case definitions.

- **Robustness_Break_Results** — sensitivity estimates using the data-driven breakpoint.

- **Robustness_Fractional_Results** — fractional-logit interaction estimates.

- **Robustness_Strict_Results** — strict-split linear-probability results.

- **Robustness_Model_Table** — publication-facing comparison of robustness estimates.

```{r inferential-robustness-checks}

# --- Inferential robustness checks ------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper for extracting one clustered model coefficient
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_clustered_coefficient <- function(
    model, cluster, coefficient, outcome, specification) {
  
  vcov_matrix <- cluster_vcov(model, cluster)
  
  cluster_degrees_freedom <- dplyr::n_distinct(cluster) - 1L
  
  cluster_contrast(
    model = model, vcov_matrix = vcov_matrix, weights =
      stats::setNames(1, coefficient), cluster_df =
      cluster_degrees_freedom, outcome = outcome, specification =
      specification, quantity = "Change in CSI slope")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Issue-area controls
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Model_Data_Issue <- Model_Data %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(issueArea))

m_phi_post2010_issue <- stats::lm(
  phi_abs ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term) + factor(issueArea), data =
    Model_Data_Issue)

m_phi_normalized_post2010_issue <- stats::lm(
  phi_normalized ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term) + factor(issueArea),
  data = Model_Data_Issue)

Robustness_Issue_Results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = m_phi_post2010_issue, cluster = Model_Data_Issue$term,
    coefficient = "csi:Post2010", outcome = "Mean absolute phi",
    specification = "OT2010 break + issue-area controls"),
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = m_phi_normalized_post2010_issue, cluster =
      Model_Data_Issue$term, coefficient = "csi:Post2010", outcome =
      "Margin-normalized phi", specification =
      "OT2010 break + issue-area controls"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Alternative definitions of a contested case
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

robustness_samples <- list(
  
  `All non-unanimous cases` = SCOTUS_NonUnanimous,
  
  `2+ minority votes` = SCOTUS_Contested,
  
  `3+ minority votes` = SCOTUS_CloselyDivided)

fit_sample_robustness <- function(
    data, sample_label, outcome) {
  
  d <- data %>% dplyr::filter(
      term >= analysis_start_term, term <= analysis_end_term, !is.na(csi),
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Post2010 = as.integer(term >= 2010))
  
  model <- stats::lm(
    stats::as.formula(
      paste0(outcome, " ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term)")), data = d
)
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = model, cluster = d$term, coefficient = "csi:Post2010", outcome =
      dplyr::case_when(
        outcome == "phi_abs" ~ "Mean absolute phi",
        outcome == "phi_normalized" ~ "Margin-normalized phi", TRUE ~
          outcome), specification =
      paste0("OT2010 break: ", sample_label))
}

Robustness_Sample_Results <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  robustness_samples, function(data, sample_label) {
    
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      
      fit_sample_robustness(
        data = data, sample_label = sample_label, outcome = "phi_abs"),
      
      fit_sample_robustness(
        data = data, sample_label = sample_label, outcome = "phi_normalized"
))
  })

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data-driven breakpoint sensitivity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

break_term_sensitivity <- Breakpoint_Best_Raw$Break_Term[
    1]

Model_Data_Break <- Model_Data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(PostBreak = as.integer(term >= break_term_sensitivity))

m_phi_databreak <- stats::lm(
  phi_abs ~ csi + csi:PostBreak + factor(term), data = Model_Data_Break)

m_phi_normalized_databreak <- stats::lm(
  phi_normalized ~ csi + csi:PostBreak + factor(term), data =
    Model_Data_Break)

Robustness_Break_Results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = m_phi_databreak, cluster = Model_Data_Break$term, coefficient =
      "csi:PostBreak", outcome = "Mean absolute phi", specification =
      paste0("Data-driven break at OT", break_term_sensitivity)),
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = m_phi_normalized_databreak, cluster = Model_Data_Break$term,
    coefficient = "csi:PostBreak", outcome = "Margin-normalized phi",
    specification =
      paste0("Data-driven break at OT", break_term_sensitivity)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fractional-logit robustness
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_phi_fractional <- stats::glm(
  phi_abs ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term), family =
    stats::quasibinomial(link = "logit"), data = Model_Data)

m_phi_normalized_fractional <- stats::glm(
  phi_normalized ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term), family =
    stats::quasibinomial(link = "logit"), data = Model_Data)

Robustness_Fractional_Results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = m_phi_fractional, cluster = Model_Data$term, coefficient =
      "csi:Post2010", outcome = "Mean absolute phi", specification =
      "Fractional logit, OT2010 break"),
  
  extract_clustered_coefficient(
    model = m_phi_normalized_fractional, cluster = Model_Data$term,
    coefficient = "csi:Post2010", outcome = "Margin-normalized phi",
    specification = "Fractional logit, OT2010 break"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strict appointing-party split as a secondary binary outcome
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Model_Data_Strict <- SCOTUS_Contested %>% dplyr::filter(
    term >= analysis_start_term, term <= analysis_end_term, !is.na(csi),
    !is.na(strict_party_split)) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    Post2010 = as.integer(term >= 2010),
    
    Strict_Split = as.integer(strict_party_split))

m_strict_lpm <- stats::lm(
  Strict_Split ~ csi + csi:Post2010 + factor(term), data = Model_Data_Strict
)

Robustness_Strict_Results <- extract_clustered_coefficient(
  model = m_strict_lpm, cluster = Model_Data_Strict$term, coefficient =
    "csi:Post2010", outcome = "Strict appointing-party split",
  specification = "Linear probability model, OT2010 break")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine results
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Robustness_Model_Results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  Robustness_Issue_Results,
  
  Robustness_Sample_Results,
  
  Robustness_Break_Results,
  
  Robustness_Fractional_Results,
  
  Robustness_Strict_Results)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication-facing robustness table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Robustness_Model_Table <- Robustness_Model_Results %>% dplyr::mutate(
    
    `95% CI` = paste0(
        sprintf("%.3f", CI_Lower), " to ", sprintf("%.3f", CI_Upper)),
    
    `p value` = dplyr::if_else(
        P_Value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", P_Value))) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    
    Outcome,
    
    Specification,
    
    Estimate = round(Estimate, 3),
    
    `Clustered SE` = round(Clustered_SE, 3),
    
    `95% CI`,
    
    `p value`)

knitr::kable(
  Robustness_Model_Table, caption =
    paste0(
      "Robustness of the changing relationship between case salience ",
      "and appointing-party alignment"
),
  booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "l", "r"))
```
